notes: **Preparation from C and H:** electric arc between carbon electrodes in hydrogen atmosphere gives acetylene: $2C + H_2 \rightarrow C_2H_2$.
**From chloroform:** $CHCl_3 + 6NaOH \xrightarrow{carbide} NaC \equiv CNa + 3NaCl + 3H_2O$, then acidify to get acetylene.

**Acidic nature:** terminal alkynes have acidic hydrogen because sp-hybridised carbon holds the lone pair tightly, stabilising the acetylide ion: $HC \equiv CH + Na \rightarrow HC \equiv CNa^+ + \frac{1}{2}H_2$.
**Reaction with Na:** $HC \equiv CH + 2Na \rightarrow NaC \equiv CNa + H_2$.
**Reaction with ammoniacal $AgNO_3$:** $HC \equiv CH + 2[Ag(NH_3)_2]^+ + 2OH^- \rightarrow AgC \equiv CAg \downarrow + 4NH_3 + 2H_2O$ (white precipitate).
